title: How far does a car go in four hours at the same speed?
description: A car covers ninety kilometres in one hundred fifty minutes, and the video finds how far it goes in four hours by changing the hours to minutes first and then cross multiplying. Keeko doubts the setup and puts four hours straight into a ratio of minutes.
teaching_notes: One idea: the two time terms of a proportion must be in the same unit before we cross multiply. Watch for students who write hours and minutes in the same proportion.

source: A car travels 90 km in 150 minutes. At the same speed, how f
video_script.why: The child sees that a proportion compares like with like, so every term of a kind must share one unit before the missing term is found.
video_script.substitution: Change the hours to minutes, set up the proportion with minutes in both time terms, then cross multiply.
video_script.anchor: the car in the book that covers 90 km in 150 minutes
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko writes one hundred fifty minutes and four hours in the same proportion, treating four as four minutes, and gets two point four kilometres.
video_script.payoff_line: The car covers one hundred forty four kilometres in four hours
maths_rules: Keeko's slip: 150 : 90 :: 4 : x gives x = 4 × 90 ÷ 150 = 2.4 km, which is less than the 90 km already covered
video_script.design: One idea: both time terms must share one unit. The proportion stays on the board and the unit labels sit under each term.

beats.on_screen: Given: 90 km in 150 minutes; the time to use is 4 hours

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the car goes ninety kilometres in one hundred fifty minutes. We want its distance in four hours.

beats.on_screen: To find: the distance in 4 hours

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the distance the car covers in four hours.

marks.prop: 150 : 90 :: 240 : x is written with minutes under both time terms

narration: <bookmark mark='conv'/>Step one, change four hours to minutes. Four times sixty is two hundred forty minutes.
<bookmark mark='prop'/>The proportion is one hundred fifty to ninety as two hundred forty to the missing distance.
<bookmark mark='cross'/>Step two, cross multiply. One hundred fifty times the distance equals two hundred forty times ninety.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Step three, find the distance. Two hundred forty times ninety is twenty one thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Dividing that by one hundred fifty gives one hundred forty four.

marks.ans: the answer is boxed and the car stops at the new marker

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The car covers one hundred forty four kilometres in four hours.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 150 : 90 :: 4 : x and x = 2.4 km; the car stops near the start; the bubble is struck through and the 4 is tagged hours against the 150 tagged minutes

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble appears with 150 : 90 :: 4 : x and x = 2.4 km
marks.short: the car stops far short of the 90 km marker
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the tags hours and minutes show the mismatch

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko writes one hundred fifty to ninety as four to the missing distance. That gives two point four kilometres.
<bookmark mark='short'/>But the car already covers ninety kilometres in one hundred fifty minutes, so four hours must give more.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>One hundred fifty is in minutes and four is in hours. We change the hours to minutes first.
